A property that varies continuously and reproducibly with temperature: liquid length, gas volume or pressure, resistance, thermocouple e.m.f.
$T/\text{K} = \theta/^\circ\text{C} + 273.15$; differences are equal in K and °C
0 K (−273.15 °C): the temperature of minimum internal energy of a system.
Triple point of water: exactly 273.16 K (0.01 °C). The scale does not depend on any substance.
Each empirical scale assumes its property is linear between the fixed points; properties differ, so scales agree only at the fixed points.
Wide range, fast response (small junction), remote reading; low and non-linear e.m.f. needs calibration.
Platinum: precise, wide range, remote reading, slower. Liquid-in-glass: cheap, direct reading, slow, limited range.
